404	    private boolean isTelephoneInUse(String normalizedTelephone) {

409	    /**
410	     * Determines whether the given already-normalized value is used by an existing owner for the
411	     * field read by {@code accessor}, comparing each existing owner's value in the same normalized
412	     * form produced by {@code normalizer}. Shared by the create-time uniqueness rules so each rule
413	     * only supplies the field to read and how to normalize it.
414	     *
415	     * @param accessor        reads the field to compare from an existing owner
416	     * @param normalizer      canonicalizes an existing owner's value into the same form as
417	     *                        {@code normalizedValue}
418	     * @param normalizedValue the already-normalized value to look for
419	     * @return {@code true} if an existing owner already uses this value
420	     */
421	    private boolean isValueInUseByExistingOwner(java.util.function.Function<Owner, String> accessor,
422	                                                java.util.function.UnaryOperator<String> normalizer,
423	                                                String normalizedValue) {
424	        if (normalizedValue == null) {
425	            return false;
426	        }
427	        return this.clinicService.findAllOwners().stream()
428	            .map(accessor)
429	            .map(normalizer)
430	            .anyMatch(normalizedValue::equals);
431	    }
432	
433	    /**
434	     * Returns the existing owners who share the given household, i.e. have the same last name and
435	     * the same address. The comparison delegates to {@link HouseholdNormalizer} so that values
436	     * differing only in letter case or in incidental whitespace are treated as the same household.
437	     *
438	     * @param lastName the last name of the owner being created
439	     * @param address  the address of the owner being created
440	     * @return the existing owners with a matching last name and address (possibly empty)
441	     */
442	    private List<Owner> sameHouseholdOwners(String lastName, String address) {
443	        String householdKey = householdNormalizer.householdKey(lastName, address);
444	        return this.clinicService.findAllOwners().stream()
445	            .filter(existing -> householdNormalizer
446	                .householdKey(existing.getLastName(), existing.getAddress()).equals(householdKey))
447	            .toList();
448	    }
449	
450	    /**
451	     * Counts the existing owners who share the given first and last name, compared
452	     * case-insensitively. Used to fix an owner's namesake count at creation time.
453	     *
454	     * @param firstName the first name of the owner being created
455	     * @param lastName  the last name of the owner being created
456	     * @return the number of existing owners with a matching first and last name
457	     */
458	    private int countNamesakes(String firstName, String lastName) {
459	        return (int) this.clinicService.findAllOwners().stream()
460	            .filter(existing -> existing.getFirstName() != null
461	                && existing.getFirstName().equalsIgnoreCase(firstName)
462	                && existing.getLastName() != null
463	                && existing.getLastName().equalsIgnoreCase(lastName))

## Summary

I implemented per-country national-number length validation for the E.164 telephone.

**The key constraint:** the seed owners (e.g. `6085551023`) are 10-digit US numbers stored without a country code. On every create, the controller normalizes each existing owner's telephone through `TelephoneNormalizer.normalize(...)` for duplicate detection. Under the default `+61` country code those legacy numbers become `+61` + 10 national digits — which violates the new `+61`=9 rule. If I'd put the strict check inside the shared `normalize` method, it would throw during comparison and break *every* create. So the strict check must apply only to the client-supplied create value, not to canonicalization of already-stored legacy data.

**Changes:**

1. `TelephoneNormalizer.java`
   - Added `NATIONAL_DIGITS_BY_COUNTRY_CODE` map (`"1"`→10, `"61"`→9). E.164 country codes are prefix-free, so at most one is a prefix of any number.
   - Added `normalizeAndValidate(String)`, which normalizes to E.164 (reusing `normalize`) and then enforces the national-number length for the recognised country code, throwing `InvalidTelephoneException` (→ 400) on a mismatch. Unknown country codes stay governed only by the generic 8–15 digit rule.
   - Kept plain `normalize(String)` lenient so it can still canonicalize legacy stored values for duplicate comparison.

2. `OwnerRestControllerV1.java`
   - `normalizeOwnerFields` now calls `normalizeAndValidate(...)` for the incoming telephone so wrong-length values are rejected with 400 on create.

The provided acceptance test `errorRejectsWrongNationalLength` (`+61 123`) passes, and the validating path also correctly rejects in-range-but-wrong-length inputs like `+61 12345678` (8 national digits) while accepting valid `+61` (9) and `+1` (10) numbers.
